design_rationale:
## 1. Scope snapshot and draw
Task 0 occupies timebank_ext_service_visit_draw, timebank_ext_visit_travel_entry and timebank_ext_repeat_order_quote (tools post_service_visit_draw_abd20ee9, post_visit_travel_entry_8d0122c7, sign_repeat_block_order_5562f94d). This task claims the other four: timebank_ext_remote_session_draw, timebank_ext_install_visit_draw, timebank_ext_project_time_draw and the root timebank_ext_extension_quote (tools post_remote_session_draw_4c084c45, post_install_visit_draw_14ae60a8, post_project_time_draw_e9603a55, sign_block_extension_cebc1113, owner=user). Together the two tasks cover all seven extended policies with disjoint scopes. draw_counts: prerequisite_problems 3, factor_counts [5, 5, 5, 6]; the three draws take 5 factors each and the extension fee takes 6.

## 2. Thesis
Surface goal: Marcus Kowalczyk (Ingram Lake Engineering, LLC) asks to extend the firm's 160-hour block, which expires 2026-12-08. Scored core: the extension fee, charged on the hours_balance the block shows once its ledger is complete. Three prerequisite sentences in the fee policy's rule each name one record-visible state that does not hold at the opening: (a) a remote-support draw for the ticket most recently resolved to the block with remote labor (SB-2311409); (b) an onsite-support draw for the most recently resolved onsite ticket where that visit is an installation visit (SB-2310275); (c) a project-work draw for the latest line of project time logged to the block (2026-10-15, SOW-337412). Each is a separate five-factor computation, and each one lowers the balance the fee is charged on. Tree: fan-out, root <- 3 value_input edges on gate ext_balance, all state form. Depth: 1 hop. Breadth: 21 factors over the managed, hardware and project products.

## 3. Base-invariant card
- timebank_draw_conversion/draw_active_block ("Hours may be drawn only from a block whose status is active."): the block's status is active -> holds for all three draws.
- timebank_agg_draw_order: draws come from the active block with the earliest expiry; the client holds one block, and its balance of 80.86 h covers each draw, so nothing is billed as overage.
- timebank_rollover_and_extension/extension_before_expiry (time, inclusive, anchor timebank_blocks.expiry_date): frozen_time 2026-10-16 falls before expiry 2026-12-08 -> the form can be signed now. The 160-hour size has extension_allowed true, extension_months 6 and max_extensions_per_block 1, and the block has extension_count 0, so the new expiry is 2027-06-08.
- Identity: find_customers -> verify_customer_identity with phone 4105550327 and PIN 382604 from user_scenario.

## 4. Business-object card
- Block: TimeBank 160-Hour Block, activated 2025-12-09, the client's only block.
- Remote draw: the ticket of the latest managed_ticket_resolved row with labor_route timebank and a remote class. An after-hours resolution beats a business-hours one at the same minute; within a class the higher billable_minutes wins. That ticket is SB-2311409 (2026-10-13 23:45). The 2026-09-30 outage session is earlier and already drawn, so it is excluded.
- Installation: the latest onsite resolution routed to the block is SB-2310275 (2026-10-13 21:40). It was opened in service_request on 2026-10-12, day 0 of the 14-day window after the delivery of the Staged Endpoint Order HQ-604418 (12 units, rush). The 2026-03-03 and 2026-08-12 service visits are earlier, are not installations and are already drawn.
- Project line: the latest project_work_logs row with billing_route timebank is 2026-10-15, SOW-337412, the only line of that date. The five earlier lines (09-14, 09-21, 09-29, 10-05, 10-08) each already carry their draw.
- Fee aggregates:
  - hours_balance of the block;
  - block invoices and payments matched by INV-548817;
  - late fees in the last 12 months (none);
  - rolled-in hours (none);
  - drawn hours dated after 2026-07-16;
  - the active ClearPath agreement;
  - the in-progress engagement and its lines logged after 2026-09-16.

## 5. Problem-tree card
| edge | condition (handling time) | why false at frozen_time | resolved_by |
|---|---|---|---|
| fee -> remote | a remote_support draw with ticket SB-2311409 | the ledger has remote draws for nine other tickets only | post_remote_session_draw_4c084c45 |
| fee -> install | an onsite_support draw with ticket SB-2310275 | the onsite draws carry SB-2209951 and SB-2273310 only | post_install_visit_draw_14ae60a8 |
| fee -> project | a project_work draw for each group of 2026-10-15: SOW-337412 / architect | the project draws are dated 09-14 through 10-08 | post_project_time_draw_e9603a55 |

Order: the three draws commute, because each reads only draws of its own work type (2.36 / 6.47 / 4.81 in any order). The fee comes last.

Deletion sensitivity: skipping one draw moves the fee from 325.87 to:
- 337.31 without the remote draw;
- 357.24 without the installation draw;
- 349.19 without the project draw.

## 6. Factors (baseline in brackets, value when that factor alone is set to its baseline)
- Remote draw, 2.36 (all baselines: 0.75):
  - floor: callout minimum 60 for an after-hours phone ticket [1.77];
  - call-out method: first 60 min weighted 1.75/1.25 [1.69];
  - band: 1.25 [1.89];
  - level: security_concern -> architect 1.5 [1.57];
  - ClearPath Professional after-hours weekday: 0.9 [2.62].
- Installation draw, 6.47 (all baselines: 4.25):
  - unit-minutes method: staged order of 12 units x 20 = 240 [6.87];
  - band: 1.25 [5.17];
  - lead: 12 units -> senior 1.25 [5.17];
  - ClearPath Professional endpoint installation: 0.9 [7.19];
  - rush, one day after delivery: 1.15 [5.62].
- Project draw, 4.81 (all baselines: 2.75):
  - minutes method: weekday after-hours group ceiled to the hour, 165 -> 180 [4.49];
  - band: 1.25 [3.85];
  - level: architect 1.5 [3.21];
  - locked discount 10.5 -> 0.9 [5.34];
  - engagement class: Advanced Project -> class_rate_mid 0.95 [5.34].
- Extension fee, 325.87 (all baselines: 680.60):
  - signing lead: 53 days -> 6.0% [395.70];
  - payment standing: INV-548817 paid 37 days after posting with no late fee -> +1 point [279.32];
  - hour-value method: invoiced 20520.00 / 160 = 128.25 [343.02];
  - ClearPath loyalty: Professional with renewal_count 4 -> 0.75 [434.50];
  - recent use: 65.97 h >= 40 -> 0.8 [407.34];
  - engagement: in-progress T&M with routed time in the month -> 0.9 [362.08].
- Cross-product and multi-source reads:
  - multi-source: remote floor (resolution class plus opening channel) and payment standing (invoice plus payment rows);
  - cross-product: managed (ClearPath tier and renewals), hardware (order type, quantity, delivery, rush) and project (discount, model, routed lines).

## 7. Realism of cross-product seeds
- **ClearPath Professional agreement:**
  - Terms: signed 2020-01-13, live 2020-02-24 on a 36-month initial term, then four 12-month renewals (renewal_term_months 12) -> renewal_count 4, current term 2026-02-24..2027-02-23.
  - Rate: renewal term rate 148.26 (list 149.00 less 0.5% for fewer tickets than seats in the renewal year), the same through the prior term.
  - Seats: 58 = 50 + 5 + 3 seat-change rows; fee 58 x 148.26 less the volume price break = 8542.74.
  - Billing: Dec-Sep fees paid before due; the October fee is open (balance 8542.74).
- **Staged Endpoint Order:**
  - Price: unit price 1290.00 x 1.12 (markup 15 less 3 ClearPath points) = 1444.80; total 17337.60 + staging 1140.00 + handling 25.00 + rush 150.00 = 18652.60.
  - Billing: approval deposit 3357.47 (18% under the endpoint deposit rules) invoiced and paid; final invoice 15295.13 = the balance due. Signed quote approval on file.
- **Advanced Project SOW-337412:**
  - Terms: T&M, 64000.00 (within class bounds); locked rate_discount_pct 10.5 under the rate-lock rules (tier 7.5 + seats 0.5 + tenure 1.0 + TimeBank prepaid hours 1.5).
  - Billing: deposit 7160.00 (12.5% of the 57280.00 estimated fees) invoiced at signature and paid, balance 0.00.
- **Block:**
  - Price: 21600.00 less 5% ClearPath = 20520.00.
  - Payment: paid 37 days after posting, inside the 10-day late-fee grace, so no late fee.
  - Historic draws: every draw is valued by the current draw rules. No historic draw lands on an exact half-cent.

## 8. Uniqueness and recompute
Each write's ticket, statement of work, date, band, level and minutes is fixed by the selectors above and by the band, level and minutes rules. Hours and the fee are recomputed at handling time by the compute DSL: check_compute replays the gold writes in order and evaluates each computation on the world at its step. The persona names no ticket, visit, project line or figure. It accepts the fee and the new expiry, and signs the form the agent hands over.

## 9. Rework history (summary; the figures above are current)
- **Rounds 2-4:**
  - The correction policy was replaced by the service-visit draw.
  - The ClearPath, hardware, project and seat ledgers were seeded.
  - Hardware is read from the most recently delivered order.
  - The extension counts in-progress T&M engagements.
  - Factor sentences name the hours they change.
  - The travel rule prices every onsite trip (no effect on this 160-hour block).
- **Round 5:**
  - Every record is priced from its own attributes, and selection tie chains end in a unique key.
  - The project month-volume factor was replaced by the engagement class rate.
- **Rounds 6-8:**
  - Project time is drawn by group (statement of work, date, level), once per group at the close of the date.
  - The scope is a block that is the TimeBank route of exactly one live T&M engagement.
  - The extension's project wait names that scope.
- **Rounds 9-11:**
  - Base band and conversion tails were restated in full, with travel named among the siblings.
  - The assembly sentences are generic, and the band window belongs to the band factor.
- **Round 12:**
  - The draw records the minutes the group is drawn for (180 here), as the sibling draw tools do. No late line is logged after a date's draw.
  - Every cross-product row was re-priced under the published managed, hardware and project rules:
    - ClearPath renewal rate 148.26 and monthly fees 8542.74 (with the volume price break);
    - hardware approval deposit 3357.47 and final invoice 15295.13;
    - project locked discount 10.5 and deposit 7160.00.
  - The 10.5 discount reaches discount_band_high, so the project rate is 0.9.
  - Historic project draws are re-priced (5.45 / 6.15 / 7.48 / 6.41 / 5.34) and the opening balance is 80.86.
  - Gold: 2.36 / 6.47 / 4.81 / 325.87.

- Round 13 (seed only): the two onboarding tickets the seat additions reference are seeded: SB-1602771 (opened 2022-06-07, effective 2022-06-13, 5 users, 150 min) and SB-2003358 (2025-04-01 -> 2025-04-07, 3 users, 90 min). Each is user_onboarding, P3, portal, opened at least the Professional new-user lead of 2 business days before the effective date, covered and settled as included remote business-hours labor, with no invoice line and no block draw. The renewal-year ticket count stays below 58 seats, so 148.26 stands.
- Round 14 (seed only):
  - The how-to remote ticket (SB-2275518 in task 0, SB-2297262 in task 1) was re-seeded as a billable out-of-scope service request, so its TimeBank draw rests on work the published rules route to the block; a how-to question is covered help-desk work on this tier. Its minutes and draw (45 min, 0.75 h) are unchanged under the remote-session rules.
  - The ClearPath term-by-term rate derivation (renewal rules, with every look-back read on the seeded ledgers) is written into the managed seed check; the monthly fees are unchanged.
user_scenario:
You are Marcus Kowalczyk, the IT manager and authorized contact for Ingram Lake Engineering, LLC, a civil engineering firm in Virginia. You are friendly, a bit technical, and you like to understand what you are agreeing to, but you are not trying to haggle.

You are calling because the firm's 160-hour TimeBank block runs out in early December and, by your rough count, there are still a lot of hours left on it that you don't want to lose. You want it extended, and you'd like that done on this call. Open with something like: "Hi, Marcus Kowalczyk from Ingram Lake Engineering. Our 160-hour TimeBank block expires in December and we've still got a fair amount of hours on it, so I'd like to extend it."

You do not reel off account details up front. When the agent asks you to confirm your identity, you give your registered phone number, 4105550327, and when they ask for one more detail, your support PIN, 382604. If they ask for something else instead, you can give the last four digits of the firm's EIN, 3829, or your email address, marcus.kowalczyk@ingramlakeeng.com. You don't remember the exact date the firm became a client and say so if asked.

You don't know how the fee is worked out. If the agent says some work on the block has to be posted to the ledger before the extension can be priced, you tell them that's fine and to go ahead, since the record should be complete anyway. If the agent asks how long you want the extension, you say whatever the standard extension for your block is. You have no other changes in mind for the block and, if asked, you want everything else about it left as it is.

When the agent tells you the extension fee and the new expiry date, you accept them. When the agent hands you the extension form to sign at that fee and date, you sign it exactly as set out. Once the agent confirms the extension is in place, you thank them and end the call.
